newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares close off on speculative selling.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares close off on speculative selling.

text.p: Brazilian stocks ended off 0.53 percent on speculative selling ahead of the upcoming options settlements, ignoring a rebound on Wall Street after Friday's sharp losses, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most traded shares fell 367 points to 68,364 points.
Volume was a moderate 321.02 million reais ($308.5 million).
"The options game set the tone of today's session," said a senior trader, adding that the market will be pretty much the same over the next four sessions as the options settle on Dec 16.
Analysts said a report by Banco Patrimonio/Salomon Brothers saying it was lowering its estimates for Telebras' earnings in 1996 and 1997 also contributed to drive share prices down.
Patrimonio said it reduced its 1996 earnings estimate on Telebras' ADRs to $8 per ADR from $8.30 and its 1997 forecast to $11.30 from $12.15.
Telebras, they noted, is the underlying stock for the most traded options.
The firm's preferred stock closed off 1.0 percent at 79 reais, while the common share fell 0.42 percent, ending at 71.40 reais.
Among other blue-chips, Petrobras preferred fell 0.64 percent to 153.50 reais at the close, while mining giant Vale do Rio Doce ended flat at 21 reais.
State power utility Eletrobras closed up 0.27 percent at 367 reais.
Despite Eletrobras' rebound, Bovespa's power sector index, comprising the nine most liquid stocks of the electrical sector, fell 0.57 percent to 1,848 points.

The Sao Paulo bourse extended today's session by 30 minutes due to an operational problem in its electronic system. The bolsa, which usually closes at 1730 local/1430 EST, closed at 1800 local/1500 EST.
